title: Alternatives in regular expressions should be grouped when used with anchors
description: When using anchors (such as ^ or $) in regular expressions, alternatives (expressions separated by the | operator) should be grouped using parentheses. Without grouping, the anchors may not apply as intended, leading to unexpected matches or bugs. Grouping ensures that the anchor applies to the entire alternation, not just the first or last alternative.
message: Group alternatives in regular expressions when using anchors to ensure the anchor applies to the entire alternation.
recommendation: Wrap the alternatives in parentheses to group them when using anchors. For example, use "^(pattern1|pattern2)$" instead of "^pattern1|pattern2$".

examples.description: Alternatives without grouping when using anchors
examples.code:
import re

# Noncompliant: anchor applies only to first alternative
pattern = r"^start|end$"
result = re.match(pattern, "start")
result2 = re.match(pattern, "end")

# Noncompliant: anchor applies only to last alternative
pattern2 = r"^start|middle|end$"

import re

# Compliant: anchor applies to entire alternation
pattern = r"^(start|end)$"
result = re.match(pattern, "start")
result2 = re.match(pattern, "end")

# Compliant: anchor applies to entire alternation
pattern2 = r"^(start|middle|end)$"

why_is_this_an_issue: When using anchors (^ or $) with alternatives in regular expressions, the anchor only applies to the first or last alternative without proper grouping. This can lead to unexpected matching behavior where the regex might match strings that do not actually start or end with the intended patterns. For example, "^start|end$" will match "start" at the beginning of a string OR "end" at the end, but it will also match "end" anywhere in the string if it is at the end, which may not be the intended behavior.
how_to_fix: Wrap the alternatives in parentheses to group them when using anchors. This ensures that the anchor applies to the entire alternation. Change "^pattern1|pattern2$" to "^(pattern1|pattern2)$" to make the anchor apply to both alternatives.
